title: CLI strips the name and falls back to 'world' when it is blank
spec: main(argv) in src/samplecli/cli.py passes the first argument to greet() verbatim, so main(['   ']) prints 'Hello,    !' and main(['  Ada\t']) prints 'Hello,   Ada\t!'. Change main() so that the first argument, when present, is stripped of surrounding whitespace (str.strip()); if the stripped result is empty (empty string or whitespace only, including tabs/newlines), use 'world' instead. With no arguments the name stays 'world'. main() still prints greet(name) and returns 0. Change only src/samplecli/cli.py. greet() in src/samplecli/greet.py must stay byte-for-byte unchanged: it does not strip and does not default (greet('') == 'Hello, !'). Do not change main()'s signature, add CLI flags, add dependencies, or edit tests. Risk: no owner_approval category applies — no signature, parameter, flag or symbol changes (not public_api) and no new dependency; this only changes CLI output for blank/padded input.

criteria.text: main(['   ']) returns 0 and prints exactly 'Hello, world!\n'
main(['']) returns 0 and prints exactly 'Hello, world!\n'
main(['\t\n ']) returns 0 and prints exactly 'Hello, world!\n'
main(['  Ada\t']) returns 0 and prints exactly 'Hello, Ada!\n'
greet() is unchanged: greet('  Ada  ') == 'Hello,   Ada  !' and greet('') == 'Hello, !'

out_of_scope: new CLI flags or argument parsing libraries
